subject: Onboarding benchmark: LumenRx acceptance & test schedule
messages:
From: Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>

Cc: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 26 Oct 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Proposed load test plan and acceptance criteria (LumenRx)

Hi Sara,

Thanks again for the sync today. As discussed, attached is a concise runbook for the onboarding benchmark and the acceptance criteria we typically use for customers on Redwood Dedicated. High-level targets:

- Sustained throughput: support 40 RPS with 512-token average payload for 30 minutes without error rate > 0.5%
- Latency: p95 <= 200 ms, p99 <= 350 ms (end-to-end token generation) under the above load
- Tail-resilience: no single-request spike > 1.5s; system-level graceful degradation to a compatible model variant if capacity constrained

Planned test items (outline):
1) Pre-test checklist (API keys, IP allowlist, sample prompt set, observed sequence lengths)
2) Baseline single-concurrency profile (smoke + warmup)
3) Ramp tests to target RPS (5m steps)
4) Soak at target for 30 minutes
5) Spike tests (2x and 5x for 1 minute)
6) Post-run diagnostics and KV cache hit analysis

Deliverables: raw perf CSV, p95/p99 plots, flamegraphs for latency contributors, and a short recommendation note if we suggest configuration changes (batching windows, quantization profile).

Can you confirm the proposed windows next week (Wed/Thu preferred) and share any constraints on IPs or test IP whitelisting? Also please attach the sample prompts you plan to use so we can pre-seed the cache accordingly.

Thanks,
Monica

All — test completed. Attaching the raw CSV and summary. Quick summary:

- Soak period (30m) @ 40 RPS, avg prompt length ~480 tokens
  - p95 end-to-end: 187 ms
  - p99 end-to-end: 338 ms
  - error rate: 0.12% (transient 429s during first 3 minutes of ramp)
- Spike to 80 RPS for 60s: p99 peaked at 620 ms, model queueing visible; we triggered graceful fallback for 40s to the smaller model variant with ~3% degradation in response fidelity
- Post-run diagnostics: KV cache hit rate ~65% after warmup; batch window average 18ms (we had configured 20ms)

Attachments included: lumenrx-load-results-20271028.csv (raw samples + per-request traces), short_signoff_lumenrx.txt (one-page signoff + recommendation).

Recommendation: Accept on performance gate — all primary targets met (p95/p99 within acceptance, error rate low). Suggest we:
- Increase burst capacity buffer for peak trading hours (reserve +20% headroom)
- Keep batch window at 20ms but enable a small dynamic bump for 95th percentile sequence lengths

Sara — if that aligns with you, Monica and Mina can produce the formal acceptance note for signatures and we’ll close the run.

Thanks everyone,
Ben
